steps.text: 4:37 P.M. \ Clear
A certain village in northern Leithanien

steps.name: Feeble Child
steps.text: *cough*, *cough*...

steps.name: Anxious Mother
steps.text: Oh, what should we do? Luca is in so much pain!

steps.name: Feeble Child
steps.text: Mama, it hurts... It hurts... My leg... My leg feels like it's on fire.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Shh, Luca. Bear with it, and keep your voice down. Thomas next door will hear you.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: You're a strong boy. One of the strongest there is! If you can't bear it, just bite the pillow.

steps.name: Anxious Mother
steps.text: He's almost chewed the cotton down to shreds! Look at how much he's sweating! He has a fever, too. We... we should take him to Dr. Marcos!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: No, we can't!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Look. Look at his leg... This black lump.

steps.name: Anxious Mother
steps.text: It's Oripathy...

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Shh, don't say it out loud. We need to keep this from Luca.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: You know what happened to Ben over at the Janiks. His arms had these lumps, and they took him away. His family hasn't seen him since.

steps.name: Anxious Mother
steps.text: *sob*... Luca... Don't let them take my Luca.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: This is how it is... We have to... endure and ride it out.

steps.name: Feeble Child
steps.text: Mama... Mamaaa...

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Here, bite Papa's hand, Luca. Hang in there... You're a big boy. You'll get better.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: A miracle will happen... A miracle will heal you up.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: We need to have faith.
Hello, is anybody home?

steps.name: Anxious Mother
steps.text: Someone's knocking on our door! They must be here to take Luca away!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Calm down. I'll take a look through the window. You and Luca stay in here. Don't come out.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Hello, sir.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: A Kuranta? Dressed up like a knight too. Not something we see in our small village every day.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Sir, please relax. We're just a few wandering doctors passing through. If it's not too much to ask, could you bring us some water?

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Water... Right, okay... If you're willing to drink the water here, I won't turn you away.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Here, you go. Leave as soon as you are finished. Take the cup with you.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: What's wrong, Liz? The water seems fine to me.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I can feel it... That silent, voiceless pain... It's right here.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Right. It's weak, but still clear as day.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Someone's screaming for help.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: If that's what you two say—

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Sir... Does someone in your family have Oripathy?

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Oripathy?! H-How dare you!

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: He's in pain, isn't he? But he hasn't given up hope.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I can... heal him.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: You... Those horns... That shape! You, and you! You are devils!

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Mister, please calm down. Just as I mentioned, we are doctors. If anyone is infected with Oripathy here, we can help alleviate their symptoms, and you don't need to give us anything in return.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: I told you—No one's sick here, and we definitely don't need any treatment!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Now leave, Kuranta! You're full of lies! And you, devils, stay far away from my house!

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Looks like he made his decision. He doesn't want us to treat his family.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It happens fairly often.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Normally, a doctor needs to earn her patient's trust, and he doesn't trust us.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: He seems nervous. It might be our race or status that's agitated him.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: If Nearl has to wave the white flag, famous and popular as she is, then Liz and I don't stand a chance. Sarkaz don't have a good reputation here.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: We could try persuading him. We've done that many times before.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We can, as long as we don't end up coming across any Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Right. It's much easier to convince a patient's family than an entire squad of Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We need to avoid that kind of 'persuasion.'

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Yeah, Liz hasn't been doing very well lately... I agree. We shouldn't take any risks.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Unfortunately, if this drags on much longer, the patient's condition will deteriorate.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Feels bad...

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Liz, are you okay? Are you feeling sick?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: That boy... He's having a really bad time... He's locked in that small room while his Oripathy torments him.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Liz is right. The kid is locked away. They're even stifling his screams.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Are they torturing an Infected?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: No, not at all. The father... He didn't show any hatred on his face when he mentioned Oripathy.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: There is hatred everywhere else.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Is he protecting the patient, then?

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: I heard the Leithanians take the Infected away from their families, round them up to live in ghettoes.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: If the patient is his child, I suppose he might be trying to hide his Infection, to keep the Gendarmerie from taking his boy away.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: He may care for his child, but that's slowly taking his child's life.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: He is losing his chance to live, and his energy is slowly draining away in this cage of love.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Hmm...

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Liz!

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Don't think about that... It'll only worsen your condition if you let that sadness get to you.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We've walked a very long distance today. I can tell you are exhausted. You need rest.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Does it feel better when you lean against me? The tent will be ready soon.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Let's start a fire and get you something to eat.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's getting dark. The Leithanian Gendarmerie moves quickly, and they might be here by tomorrow. We should leave this place before do, if we want to stay out of trouble.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Right, it's not a good idea to show ourselves to the Gendarmerie.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Liz, lie down here, closer to the fire. It'll warm you up.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Yeah.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You two should get some rest. I'll stand watch.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's the Gendarmerie. They're here.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Shining, are you awake already? You went to bed not that long ago.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I got enough sleep. We need to leave right now. Liz, can you walk?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Yeah, I can.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Ughh...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You look really pale. Did you get enough rest?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I... I'm okay. I just feel a little dizzy.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: The Gendarmerie went straight to the house we visited last night. Shining, should we really just leave like this?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: There's a good hiding spot behind the bushes.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: They won't spot us there.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Nearl, hold Liz. If it looks like things are getting out of hand, do as you see fit.

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: Mr. Reiss! Please open the door!

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: Mr. Reiss!

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: Officer, look! I told you something's not right with Old Reiss's family!

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: His boy—his name is Luca—he was playing in the fields a few days ago, and he suddenly got sick after he came back.

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: For the few days after that, his family kept themselves locked inside, and they wouldn't come out, no matter what!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: I-I'm just taking care of Luca...

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: How am I supposed to believe you?! What kind of disease would keep a strong kid like him bedridden for days on end?

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: Besides, if your kid really caught a cold, you could've taken him to Dr. Marcos!

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: Something sounds fishy here.

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: Right, officer? I am doing this for everyone's safety!

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: This is a peaceful, quiet village. We can't let Oripathy ruin our lives here!

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: Right, all Infected must be quarantined at a nearby quarantine zone.

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: Right? Reiss, did you hear that? Your boy's just going to the quarantine zone! Luca will be in good hands there! Much better than keeping him here!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: But what, Mr. Reiss? You will need to open this door today.

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Yeah, Papa, open the door.

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: I'm starving. I want bread. And not just one slice. I can eat five or six slices in one go.

steps.name: Nervous Neighbor
steps.text: Huh—Huh?!

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Oh, Uncle Thomas. Sorry for bumping into you. I'm in a rush to get home for breakfast so Mama doesn't give me a scolding.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Oh, Luca, you're home at last. What took you so long?

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: I'm very sorry, Officer. This is my boy, Luca. It's not that I didn't want to open up. He really wasn't home.

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: This boy is Luca? He looks as fit as a fiddle. Is he really sick?

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: *cough*, just a little cold. You know boys his age. They get sick after a day of fun and games.

steps.name: Leithanian Gendarmerie
steps.text: I suppose so. I've met plenty of Infected. None of them are nearly as lively. Dr. Marcos, what do you think?

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: Oh... Oh? You want me to check him? Let me take a look.

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: Look at how muscular and sweaty his arms are. So sturdy to the feel.

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: And his legs...

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: *Cough*

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: My, what strong legs. There's so much mud. Looks like this boy has been having fun.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Sorry for all the trouble, Dr. Marcos.

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: Oh, no need to worry! Officer, we've been working all morning. I'm as famished as one can be, My vision is starting to blur.

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: Perhaps we should let the boy go home for his breakfast?

steps.name: Elderly Doctor
steps.text: Don't worry, if little Luca gets sick again, I will check on him, and if anything's amiss, I will let you know right away.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Phew... Thank goodness.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Luca, my boy! Let Papa look at you!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: You're... fine? You can run all over the place, and you can eat...

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: These crystals... They are still here, but they're much smaller now. Not nearly as swollen anymore. You've gotten much better. No wonder Dr. Marcos didn't notice.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: I-Is this a miracle?

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Papa, it isn't a miracle. A fowlbeast healed me!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: A fowlbeast...?

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: It was a really, really pretty fowlbeast! Its feathers were so much bluer than the water in the lake! I've never seen a little fowlbeast so beautiful!

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Last night, it flew into my room through the window, and settled by my pillow.

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: There was a white light around the tiny fowlbeast. It was so bright and warm...

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: It came over me, and I stopped hurting right away.

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: A small fowlbeast? And one that glowed?

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: Yeah! I'm not lying!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: My boy, you were ill. You were probably hallucinating.

steps.name: Lively Child
steps.text: It wasn't! It sang a song too! I heard it! The blue fowlbeast sang a song for me!

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Okay, okay. Everything's fine now. It's all okay...

steps.name: Helpless Father
steps.text: Thank you, blue, magical fowlbeast. I have no idea if you were real or not—you definitely weren't—but whichever the case, thank you for giving Luca a pleasant dream.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We should get going.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: You aren't mad, are you...?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Why would I be mad about a little blue bird checking on a sickly boy at night?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Oh, right, the bird was glowing in the dark, too.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: *cough*, *cough*.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Sorry, Shining, Liz just couldn't fall asleep last night, so I...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining, I was the one who asked Nearl to help me treat the boy.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I couldn't fall asleep otherwise... I could hear the boy's pained cries in my head.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: If it wasn't for my legs... if they had some strength left in them... I would've gone myself.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Please don't blame Nearl.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You don't have to apologize. We are doctors. You two did what you should've done.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: I didn't expect the Gendarmerie to show up today, though... I wonder what will happen to the boy and his family in the future.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: They may get to live out the rest of their lives in peace, or they might have to move in the not-so-distant future.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: As doctors, we may be able to treat our patients' pain, but we don't have any way to treat their predicaments.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I know that, Shining, but I couldn't spend so much time thinking about it.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: The boy... was really hurting all over.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: When I looked at him, I felt the same pain myself.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: All I knew how to do was... help him hurt less.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I wanted to help him... to ease his pain... I wanted to help him leave that room... to help him run and jump again.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Liz, I just have one question. Look at me and answer me. Do you think this is really necessary?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: What do you mean... necessary?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Just like what happened before.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: What happened before... No, I don't want to be like before.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: At the time, they were coming for me. I was locked... I had nowhere to go. I had to heal them.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But what about now?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Now... I'm going everywhere to find them.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I can feel the pain of those who are sick and hurt, and I don't want them hurt anymore.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I stretch my hands out to them... to embrace their pain. I have my birdie sing in their ears.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I never expected the boy would see my birdie. He seemed so happy in his sleep.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: When that happened, those shards that tied me down were gone... Birdie's steps became much lighter too.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Is that what it means to be happy? Shining, it sounds like I'm happy too.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Okay... That's the answer I wanted.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Yes, Liz. That's what it means to be happy. You know what it means to be happy now.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Really? So this is how it's like to be happy. So now I... Mmm...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Does it make your heart ache?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Yes, Shining... It really makes my heart ache.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Why is this happening to Liz? She doesn't have the strength to stand up.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: This is the outcome of her choice.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Because she treated the kid last night...?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Yes, her condition was hardly optimal to begin with. Even the use of simple healing Arts takes its toll on her. Not to mention she was treating acute Oripathy. She's nearing her limits.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: If I knew this was going to happen...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: If you knew, would you have stopped her?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: This is what I wanted to do... I wanted to heal the boy.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: See? This is what Liz wanted, even though it left her exhausted.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Right... I guess I wouldn't have been able to stop her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Exactly. This is a choice, and these are the choices you two have made. Like Liz, you always choose to sacrifice yourself to treat someone else's pain, whether visible or not.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: I should've... respected your decisions.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Shining...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: But my hope is that... Liz will have more choices available to her.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: And you too, Margaret. My hope is that you will have more choices too.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: What does it mean to have more choices?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: You've always wanted to see the world outside, don't you, Liz?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Yes, that's my greatest wish, Shining. I've been to so many places with you and Nearl.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: These places are beautiful... Hatred and pain sometimes engulf these skies and lands, but that doesn't change the beauty that lies underneath.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I... I still want to see much more, and not just what the bird sings to me.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Yes, it's time we expand our horizons.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: It sounds like you just made a decision, Shining.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Nearl, do you remember the pharmaceutical company that the patient we treated last time mentioned?

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: You mean... Rhodes Island?

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Yes, Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We've been wandering the world all these years. How many patients have we treated altogether?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: I don't remember...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: It's okay if you don't remember, but, Liz, do you want to treat even more people out there?

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Yes... I want to.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Okay. What about you, Nearl?

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: Rhodes Island, is it...? No objections here.

steps.name: Nearl
steps.text: I trust you, and I trust your decision. If that's where Liz wants to go, then we'll take her there.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: We'll be together...

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: Together.

steps.name: Shining
steps.text: We've made our decision. Let's go, then.

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: Let's go...

steps.name: Nightingale
steps.text: ...to Rhodes Island.
